cls: Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK) inhibitor - small molecule kinase inhibitor
quick: CLL/SLL and Waldenstrom: 420 mg orally once daily
Take with a glass of water; with or without food; swallow whole
Can cause fetal harm; avoid - use effective contraception
Avoid breastfeeding during and for 1 week after therapy
No adjustment in mild-moderate; avoid/caution in severe (CrCl <30)
Reduce dose in mild-moderate; avoid in severe impairment
No direct interaction; avoid excess due to bleeding risk
CBC, bleeding, atrial fibrillation/BP, infection, second cancers
summary: Ibrutinib is an oral covalent inhibitor of Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK) used to treat B-cell malignancies including chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL)/small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL), Waldenstrom's macroglobulinemia, and chronic graft-versus-host disease. By blocking BTK signaling it impairs malignant B-cell survival, proliferation, and trafficking. Key toxicities are hemorrhage, atrial fibrillation, cytopenias, hypertension, and infections, requiring close monitoring and dose interruption around surgery.
indications: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) / small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL), including with 17p deletion
Chronic graft-versus-host disease (cGVHD) after failure of one or more lines of systemic therapy (adults and pediatric patients >=1 year)

dosage.n: Continue until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity
After failure of >=1 line of systemic therapy

admin: Take orally at about the same time each day with a glass of water
Swallow capsules/tablets whole - do not open, break, crush, or chew
May be taken with or without food
Avoid grapefruit and Seville oranges (CYP3A inhibition)
Hold therapy 3-7 days before and after surgery depending on bleeding risk
moa: Ibrutinib is a small-molecule inhibitor of Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK). It forms a covalent bond with a cysteine residue in the BTK active site, irreversibly inhibiting BTK enzymatic activity. BTK is a signaling molecule of the B-cell antigen receptor and cytokine receptor pathways; its inhibition blocks B-cell proliferation, survival, trafficking, chemotaxis, and adhesion, leading to malignant B-cell death.

relative: Active serious bleeding or recent major surgery
Concurrent warfarin or strong CYP3A inhibitors/inducers (avoid or adjust)

preg: Based on animal data, ibrutinib can cause fetal harm. Advise females of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose. Males with female partners should use contraception during and for 1 week after therapy.
lact: Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in a breastfed child, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose.
renal: No dose adjustment is needed for mild to moderate renal impairment (CrCl >=30 mL/min); maintain hydration. There are limited data and no specific dosing for severe renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min) or patients on dialysis - use only if benefit outweighs risk.
hepatic: Hepatically metabolized via CYP3A. Reduce dose in mild (Child-Pugh A) and moderate (Child-Pugh B) impairment per labeling; ibrutinib is not recommended in severe (Child-Pugh C) hepatic impairment.

major: Strong CYP3A inhibitors (ketoconazole, clarithromycin, ritonavir) - markedly increase ibrutinib levels; avoid or reduce dose
Strong CYP3A inducers (rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin) - reduce ibrutinib efficacy; avoid
Warfarin and other vitamin K antagonists - increased bleeding risk; avoid co-administration
moderate: Moderate CYP3A inhibitors (fluconazole, erythromycin, diltiazem) - reduce ibrutinib dose
Antiplatelet agents and NSAIDs (additive bleeding risk)
minor: Drugs that may add to QT/arrhythmia considerations
interactions.food: Grapefruit juice and Seville oranges inhibit CYP3A and increase ibrutinib exposure - avoid
interactions.alcohol: No direct interaction; minimize to limit additive bleeding/GI risk
interactions.diagnostics: May cause cytopenias, raised liver enzymes, hyperuricemia, and increased creatinine

serious: Serious infections (including opportunistic, PJP, fungal, viral reactivation)
Second primary malignancies (skin and other cancers)

monitoring: CBC monthly and as clinically indicated (cytopenias)
Cardiac rhythm and blood pressure; ECG if arrhythmia suspected
Signs of infection; consider antimicrobial prophylaxis in at-risk patients
Periodic skin examinations for second malignancies
Liver function and hepatitis B status before starting
counsel: Take one dose each day at the same time, swallowing whole with water
Report unusual bruising, bleeding, blood in stool/urine, or severe headache
Report palpitations, dizziness, shortness of breath, or fainting
Report fever or signs of infection promptly
Tell your doctor before any surgery or dental procedure
Use effective contraception and do not breastfeed
pk: Rapid BTK occupancy after dosing; clinical response over weeks to months
Plasma peak (Tmax) reached approximately 1-2 hours after oral dose
Approximately 4-13 hours (terminal); BTK inhibition outlasts plasma levels
Sustained BTK inhibition supports once-daily dosing
Store at 20-25 C (excursions 15-30 C); keep in original container
pearls: Hold ibrutinib 3-7 days before and after surgery to reduce bleeding risk
New-onset atrial fibrillation is a hallmark cardiac toxicity - check pulse/ECG
Early lymphocytosis (redistribution) can occur and is not treatment failure
Strong CYP3A inhibitors/inducers and grapefruit dramatically alter exposure
Avoid warfarin; use alternative anticoagulation with caution if needed
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as possible on the same day, then resume the normal schedule the next day. Do not take an extra dose to make up for a missed one.
overdose: There is no specific antidote. Doses above the recommended level may increase toxicity (e.g., bleeding, cytopenias, cardiac effects). Manage with discontinuation, supportive care, and monitoring; dialysis is unlikely to be useful given high protein binding.
